sections.overview: The Fulvous-breasted Woodpecker is a resident Asian woodpecker occurring from the Indian subcontinent into parts of Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: It has strongly barred black-and-white upperparts and a buff-toned breast; the male has a red crown, unlike the female.
sections.habitat: It uses open wooded country, broad-leaved woodland, forest clearings and trees along roads, including varied habitats across Bangladesh.
sections.diet: Its recorded foods include insect grubs, other insects, fruit pulp and nectar, which it takes while pecking at tree trunks.
sections.behavior: This diurnal species is usually seen in pairs or small groups working over trees, and it is described as sedentary in Bangladesh.
sections.reproduction: Bangladesh records report breeding in April and May. The sources consulted do not provide a confirmed clutch size or a detailed account of nest construction.
sections.ecology: By searching trunks for animal prey and also taking fruit and nectar, it uses several food resources in wooded landscapes.
sections.conservation: The Bangladesh species account reports that its population size and trend are unknown, so it does not establish a local trend.
